minor.issue: PB-003 signals (almost_ambassador, recommend_specialist, support_deal — impact 5-7) do NOT surface for client demo because deterministic actions (use_benefit=9, docs_for_benefit=8, activate_twin=8, house_health=7) exhaust top-3 slots. Problem statement says 'almost_ambassador should appear since remaining=1' — currently it doesn't reach next_action nor secondary[:2]. Consider (a) reserving one slot for PB-003 community actions, or (b) raising impact of PB-003 signals to be competitive, or (c) returning more than 3 candidates so UI can pick relevant ones.

integration_issues.issue: Anonymous visitor to /marketplace is redirected to landing by ServiceGate(serviceId='specialisti') — same behavior as iter168. Backend delivers correct extended trust fields (verified in pytest). PublicMarketplace never mounts for anon/client in demo env; would need specialist/admin session to see it — outside PB-003 scope but blocks direct UI verification.

action_items: Raise PB-003 candidate impact in propbenefits/ai_agents.py::success_manager so almost_ambassador (currently 6) and recommend_specialist (currently 7) can reach top-3 for engaged clients — otherwise the promise 'AI Success Manager mentions: recommend specialist, benefit earned, one step to Ambassador, deal needs N supporters' is not visible to users with many deterministic hooks active.

OPTIONAL / pre-existing (iter168): ServiceGate('specialisti') redirects logged-in client and anonymous away from /marketplace in demo env — prevents UI trust-badge verification. Backend confirmed correct.
critical_code_review_comments: propbenefits/ai_agents.py::success_manager returns only next_action + secondary[:2] = 3 items. When many deterministic actions are eligible, PB-003 community actions (impact 5-7) are ALWAYS crowded out. Recommend: return `pb_community: candidates_pb003[:1]` as a separate slot so recommend/ambassador/deal signals always have visibility.

propbenefits/trust_engine.py::signal_deal uses $addToSet for signals list — good (idempotent). But no cap on how many signals a single user can toggle across all deals — potential abuse vector. Non-issue for MVP.
propbenefits/trust_engine.py::sync_trust_graph runs delete_many + insert_many on every tick. On large datasets edges collection is fully rebuilt — OK for MVP but consider incremental sync at scale.
propbenefits/trust_engine.py::trust_score uses ObjectId.is_valid(specialist_id) guard but then passes a `None` inside $or if invalid — Mongo tolerates it, but explicit branch would be cleaner.
routes/prop_benefits.py::specialist_trust does not verify specialist_id belongs to an actual specialist — returns score=0 for any string. Consider 404 for unknown ids to help clients.

rca of the issue: Success Manager PB-003 signal invisibility: ai_agents.py:118 sorts all candidates by impact DESC and returns only next_action + secondary[:2]. For client demo, deterministic candidates use_benefit(9) + docs_for_benefit(8) + activate_twin(8) + house_health(7) + claim_opportunity(7) all fire, pushing recommend_specialist(7) and almost_ambassador(6) below the top-3 cutoff. Fix options: (1) increase impact of PB-003 signals (almost_ambassador should be 9 when remaining=1 — 'one step from ambassador' is arguably the highest-value nudge), (2) reserve a dedicated 'community' slot in the response payload, (3) return top-5 and let UI pick 3.
